children.name: Herpetotheres
children.description: A Neotropical monotypic genus of specialised snake-hunting falcon. The laughing falcon's oversized head and black mask give it an almost comical appearance, but its precision in decapitating venomous serpents is deadly serious.

children.name: Herpetotheres cachinnans
children.description: The laughing falcon (Herpetotheres cachinnans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Micrastur
children.description: Secretive Neotropical forest falcons built for manoeuvring through dense jungle understorey — short rounded wings and a long tail let them weave through branches in pursuit of lizards, birds, and small mammals. Most species have bare facial skin and are heard far more often than seen.

children.name: Micrastur ruficollis
children.description: The barred forest falcon (Micrastur ruficollis) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It occurs from southern Mexico south through most of Central America and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

children.name: Micrastur plumbeus
children.description: The plumbeous forest-falcon (Micrastur plumbeus) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae only found in the Chocó region in Colombia and Ecuador. This rare bird has not been often spotted, which makes its study complicated. For a long time, it was considered to be part of the lined forest-falcons but it now known to be a species of its own. It is currently considered a vulnerable species because of the precarity of its habitat that is threatened by deforestation.

children.name: Micrastur gilvicollis
children.description: The lined forest falcon (Micrastur gilvicollis) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

children.name: Micrastur mintoni
children.description: The cryptic forest falcon (Micrastur mintoni) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae. It is found in the southeastern Amazon rainforest in Brazil and Bolivia. While uncommon in its Amazonian range, it remains widespread and is therefore rated as least concern by BirdLife International and IUCN. Unlike the lined forest falcon, with which it has long been confused in a cryptic species complex, adult cryptic forest falcons only have a single white tail-band (in addition to a narrow white tail-tip).

children.name: Micrastur mirandollei
children.description: The slaty-backed forest falcon (Micrastur mirandollei) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons, and caracaras. It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

children.name: Micrastur semitorquatus
children.description:
The collared forest falcon (Micrastur semitorquatus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae. It is the largest member of the Micrastur genus and a common inhabitant of tropical rainforests in Latin America. Hiding in the dense forest canopy, they are a secretive bird often only recognized by their distinctive call. With a morphology or body type allowing them to be agile in their forested habitat, their diet comprises a wide variety of prey from smaller frogs (20 g) to adult turkeys (2.7-3.2 kg).
Nesting occurs mainly in the cavities of Spanish cedar trees, which are also a key species exploited by the local logging industry. This is a potential conservation concern for the collared forest falcon.

children.name: Micrastur buckleyi
children.description: Buckley's forest falcon (Micrastur buckleyi), also called lesser collared forest-falcon and Traylor's forest-falcon, is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Colombia and Venezuela.

children.name: Spiziapteryx
children.description: The smallest member of the caracara lineage, this Argentine and Uruguayan endemic resembles a miniature falcon with cryptic grey, white, and black spotted plumage. It hunts insects and lizards from exposed perches in dry woodland and savanna.

children.name: Spiziapteryx circumcincta
children.description:
The spot-winged falconet (Spiziapteryx circumcincta) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Falconinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, and possibly Uruguay.
The spot-winged falconet is the only member of genus Spiziapteryx and has no subspecies. Though by size and shape it appears to be a typical falcon, genetic data place it closer to the caracaras.

children.name: Caracara
children.description: Large, long-legged caracaras of open country, instantly recognisable by their flat-crowned heads, heavy hooked bills, and bare orange-red facial skin. They stride across the ground like corvids, omnivorously scavenging and hunting in a manner unique among raptors.

children.name: Caracara cheriway
children.description: The crested caracara (Caracara plancus) is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae.

children.name: Caracara plancus

children.name: Daptrius
children.description: Two distinctive Neotropical caracaras united by bare facial skin and a taste for wasp brood and fruit alongside carrion and small prey. They are bold, social, and among the noisiest raptors in the Amazon, often encountered in family groups.

children.name: Daptrius americanus
children.description:
The red-throated caracara (Ibycter americanus) is a social species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae. It is placed in the monotypic genus Ibycter, or sometimes united in Daptrius with the black caracara. Unique among caracaras, it mainly feeds on the larvae of bees and wasps, but also takes the adult insects and fruits and berries.
It is found from far southern Mexico through parts of Central and South America south to Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Milvago
children.description: Smaller, paler caracaras of open lowland country, with a more slender build and a less imposing bill than their crested relatives. Both species are bold commensals of human habitation, often seen scavenging around farms, towns, and refuse dumps.

children.name: Milvago chimachima
children.description: Milvago chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara) is a typical caracaras species found in North America and South America regions.

children.name: Milvago chimango
children.description: The chimango caracara (Daptrius chimango), also known as chimango or tiuque, is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Phalcoboenus
children.description: Andean and Patagonian mountain caracaras — robust, long-legged birds of high-altitude grasslands and wind-scoured coasts with striking pied or barred plumage and bare yellow facial skin. They are bold and inquisitive, sometimes approaching hikers in search of scraps.

children.name: Phalcoboenus carunculatus
children.description: The carunculated caracara (Daptrius carunculatus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Phalcoboenus megalopterus
children.description: The mountain caracara (Daptrius megalopterus), (Spanish: corequenque) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae.

children.name: Phalcoboenus albogularis
children.description: Phalcoboenus albogularis (White-throated Caracara) is a mountain caracaras species found in South America region.

children.name: Phalcoboenus australis
children.description: The striated caracara (Daptrius australis), also known as Forster's caracara, is a Near Threatened bird of prey of the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Phalcoboenus chimango
children.description: Phalcoboenus chimango (Chimango Caracara) is a falconidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Falco
children.description: The archetypal birds of prey — streamlined, pointed-winged, lightning-fast. The tomial tooth on the upper mandible severs prey's spinal cord on impact. Five species breed in Sweden regularly, from the hovering kestrel of roadsides to the peregrine reclaiming Stockholm's tower blocks.

children.name: Falco naumanni
children.description: The lesser kestrel (Falco naumanni) is a small falcon.

children.name: Falco tinnunculus
children.description: The common kestrel, also known as the European kestrel, Eurasian kestrel or Old World kestrel, is a species of predatory bird belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".

children.name: Falco newtoni
children.description: The Malagasy kestrel (Falco newtoni), also known as the Madagascar kestrel, Malagasy spotted kestrel, Newton's kestrel, Madagascar spotted kestrel, katiti (Creole) or hitsikitsika (Malagasy), is a small bird of prey of the genus Falco.

children.name: Falco punctatus
children.description: Falco punctatus (Mauritius Kestrel) is a kestrels species found in Africa region.

children.name: Falco araea
children.description: The Seychelles kestrel (Falco araeus) is a small bird of prey belonging to the genus Falco in the falcon family, Falconidae.

children.name: Falco moluccensis
children.description: The spotted kestrel (Falco moluccensis), also known as the Moluccan kestrel, is a falcon found throughout Indonesia and Timor-Leste.

children.name: Falco cenchroides
children.description: The nankeen kestrel (Falco cenchroides), also known as the Australian kestrel, is a raptor native to Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Falco sparverius
children.description: The American kestrel (Falco sparverius) is the smallest and most common falcon in North America.

children.name: Falco rupicoloides
children.description: The greater kestrel (Falco rupicoloides) or white-eyed kestrel is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco alopex
children.description: The fox kestrel (Falco alopex) is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco ardosiaceus
children.description: The grey kestrel (Falco ardosiaceus) is an African bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco dickinsoni
children.description: Dickinson's kestrel (Falco dickinsoni) is a bird of prey of southern and eastern Africa belonging to the falcon family Falconidae. It is named after John Dickinson, an English physician and missionary who collected the type specimen. It is also known as the white-rumped kestrel. Its closest relatives are the grey kestrel and banded kestrel and the three are sometimes placed in the subgenus Dissodectes.

children.name: Falco zoniventris
children.description: The banded kestrel (Falco zoniventris) is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco rupicolus
children.description: The rock kestrel (Falco rupicolus) is a bird of prey species belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco duboisi
children.description: The Réunion kestrel (Falco duboisi) is an extinct bird of prey which belongs to the falcon family. It was endemic to the Mascarene island of Réunion and was part of the Western Indian Ocean radiation of kestrels.

children.name: Falco chicquera
children.description: The red-necked falcon (Falco chicquera) is a bird of prey in the falcon family with two disjunct populations, one in India and the other in Africa. This medium-sized falcon has bluish grey wings and upper body, a chestnut red cap with short chin straps passing through the eye. The primary feathers of the wing are black and a single black band at the tip of the tail are distinctive. The Indian subspecies Falco chicquera chicquera also known as the red-headed merlin or red-headed falcon is found mainly in the open plains of the India Subcontinent although it is thought to have occurred further west in southeastern Iran. The subspecies Falco chicquera ruficollis found in sub-Saharan Africa is sometimes treated as a full species, the rufous-necked falcon (Falco ruficollis), on the basis of its well-separated geographic range and distinctive pattern. It appears very similar to the Indian form but has dark barring on the upperparts, a rufous breast band, and black moustachial and eye stripes. As in most falcons, the females are larger and falconers in India called the female turumti and the male as chatwa. They hunt in pairs mostly at dawn and dusk, capturing small birds, bats and squirrels.

children.name: Falco vespertinus
children.description: The red-footed falcon, formerly the western red-footed falcon, is a bird of prey. It belongs to the family Falconidae, the falcons. This bird is found in eastern Europe and Asia although its numbers are dwindling rapidly due to habitat loss and hunting.

children.name: Falco amurensis
children.description: The Amur falcon (Falco amurensis) is a small raptor of the falcon family.

children.name: Falco eleonorae
children.description: Eleonora's falcon (Falco eleonorae) is a medium-sized falcon. It belongs to the hobby group, a rather close-knit number of similar falcons often considered a subgenus Falco. The sooty falcon is sometimes considered its closest relative, but while they certainly belong to the same lineage, they do not seem to be close sister species. The English name and the species name eleonorae commemorate Eleanor of Arborea, Queen or Lady-Judge (Juighissa) and national heroine of Sardinia, who in 1392, under the jurisdiction conferred by the Carta de Logu, became the first ruler in history to grant protection to hawk and falcon nests against illegal hunters. The genus name Falco is from Late Latin falx, falcis, a sickle, referring to the claws of the bird.

children.name: Falco concolor
children.description: The sooty falcon (Falco concolor) is a medium-sized falcon, breeding from northeastern Africa to the southern Persian Gulf region, and wintering in East Africa (Mozambique, eastern South Africa) and Madagascar.

children.name: Falco columbarius
children.description: The merlin is a small species of falcon from the Northern Hemisphere, with numerous subspecies throughout North America and Eurasia. A bird of prey, the merlin breeds in the northern Holarctic; some migrate to subtropical and northern tropical regions in winter. Males typically have wingspans of 53–58 centimetres (21–23 in), with females being slightly larger.

children.name: Falco rufigularis
children.description: The bat falcon (Falco rufigularis) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It is found in Mexico, Central America, Trinidad, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

children.name: Falco deiroleucus
children.description: The orange-breasted falcon (Falco deiroleucus) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. It is found in southern Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Panama, and in all South American countries except Chile and Uruguay, though in Argentina only in the far northwest. Despite its wide range, it is scarce, and considered by IUCN to be Near Threatened.

children.name: Falco femoralis
children.description: The aplomado falcon (Falco femoralis) is a medium-sized falcon of the Americas.

children.name: Falco subbuteo
children.description: The Eurasian hobby, or just hobby, is a small, slim falcon. It belongs to a group of similar falcons often considered a subgenus of Falco.

children.name: Falco cuvierii
children.description: The African hobby (Falco cuvierii) is a small species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco severus
children.description: The Oriental hobby (Falco severus) is a species of falcon typically 27–30 cm long.

children.name: Falco longipennis
children.description: The Australian hobby (Falco longipennis), also known as the little falcon, is one of six Australian members of the family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco berigora
children.description: Falco berigora (Brown Falcon) is a brown falcons species found in Australia region.

children.name: Falco novaeseelandiae
children.description: The New Zealand falcon is New Zealand's only falcon, and one of only four living native and two endemic birds of prey. It is frequently mistaken for the larger and more common swamp harrier. It is the country's most threatened bird of prey, with only around 5000–15000 individuals remaining. Under the New Zealand Threat Classification System the falcon is stable at Threatened, with conservation research needed. The kārearea was voted Bird of the Year winner in the annual Forest & Bird competition in 2012 and again in 2025.

children.name: Falco hypoleucos
children.description: The grey falcon (Falco hypoleucos) is a medium-sized falcon native to Australia, possibly the rarest.

children.name: Falco subniger
children.description: The black falcon (Falco subniger) is a medium-large falcon that is endemic to Australia.

children.name: Falco biarmicus
children.description: The lanner falcon (Falco biarmicus) is a medium-sized bird of prey that breeds in Africa, southeast Europe and just into Asia.

children.name: Falco jugger
children.description: Falco jugger (Laggar Falcon) is a hierofalcons species found in Asia region.

children.name: Falco cherrug
children.description: The saker falcon (Falco cherrug) is a large falcon species.

children.name: Falco rusticolus
children.description:
The gyrfalcon, also abbreviated as gyr, is a bird of prey in the genus Falco (falcons and kestrels) and the largest species of the family Falconidae. A high-latitude species, the gyrfalcon breeds on the Arctic coasts and tundra, the islands of northern North America and Siberia, where it is mainly a resident species. Some gyrfalcons disperse more widely after the breeding season or in winter, and individual vagrancy can take birds for long distances. Its plumage varies with location, with birds being coloured from all-white to dark brown. These colour variations are called morphs. Like other falcons, it shows sexual dimorphism, with the female much larger than the male.
For centuries, the gyrfalcon has been valued as a hunting bird. Typical prey includes the ptarmigan and waterfowl, which it may attack in flight; and it also hunts fish and small mammals.

children.name: Falco mexicanus
children.description: Falco mexicanus (Prairie Falcon) is a hierofalcons species found in North America region.

children.name: Falco peregrinus
children.description: The peregrine falcon, also referred to simply as the peregrine, is a bird of prey (raptor) in the family Falconidae known for its speed. A large, crow-sized falcon, it has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts and a black head. As is typical for bird-eating (avivore) raptors, peregrine falcons are sexually dimorphic, with females being considerably larger than males.

children.name: Falco pelegrinoides
children.description: The Barbary falcon (Falco peregrinus pelegrinoides) is a non-migratory subspecies of the peregrine falcon found from the Canary Islands eastwards across some parts of North Africa to the Middle East.

children.description: The Taita falcon (Falco fasciinucha) is a small falcon found in central and eastern Africa.
